# opencode-invalid-request-fix

**One-command fix for OpenCode sessions that die forever with `Error: Invalid request parameters`.**

Two different causes are covered:

| # | Cause | Symptom | Fix in this repo |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **NUL bytes (`\x00`) in conversation history** | `400` + `"String must not contain null bytes"` — every later message in that session fails | `nul-sanitizer` plugin strips them before every model call |
| 2 | **Removed / deprecated model** | `410` + `"Model X has been deprecated."` | plugin auto-switches the session to your configured default model and retries |

Both of these are *sticky*: once they happen, the session is unusable and "continue" does not help,
because the bad state is stored in the session history.

---

## Install

### One-liner (recommended)

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CanArslanDev/opencode-invalid-request-fix/main/install.sh | bash
```

### From a clone

```sh
git clone https://github.com/CanArslanDev/opencode-invalid-request-fix.git
cd opencode-invalid-request-fix
./install.sh
```

Installing is idempotent. Existing files are backed up first (`*.bak.<timestamp>`).

### Optional flags

```sh
./install.sh --model venice/deepseek-v4-1-flash-uncensored   # also set a default model
./install.sh --no-agents                                     # skip the AGENTS.md guidance block
./install.sh --dry-run                                       # show what would happen
./install.sh --prefix ~/.config/opencode                     # custom config dir
```

---

## What gets installed

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `<config>/plugins/nul-sanitizer.ts` | The fix. Hooks `prompt`, `context`, `compaction`, `generate`, `title` and `retry`. |
| `<config>/scripts/fix-nul-bytes.py` | Permanent DB cleanup for sessions that already contain NULs. |
| `<config>/AGENTS.md` | A managed block telling the agent to filter binary output at the source. |
| `<config>/nul-sanitizer.log` | Runtime diagnostics (created on first use; silence with `OPENCODE_NUL_QUIET=1`). |

`<config>` is `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/opencode`.

### `/fix-nuls` command

The plugin also registers a TUI command:

```
/fix-nuls         # permanently clean NULs from the session database (takes a backup first)
/fix-nuls dry     # report only, change nothing
```

You do **not** need it for the fix to work — the plugin sanitizes on the fly. It is only for
housekeeping so stored history stays small and clean.

---

## How it works

The plugin runs inside the OpenCode **server** and hooks the moment right before a request is
dispatched. It walks `event.messages` and `event.system` and replaces any `\u0000` with a space.
Persisted history is not rewritten, so **old broken sessions become usable again** too.

```ts
await ctx.session.hook("context", onRequest)  // agent loop
await ctx.session.hook("compaction", onRequest)
await ctx.session.hook("generate", onRequest)
await ctx.session.hook("title", onRequest)
await ctx.session.hook("retry", onRetry)      // 400 → retry, 410 → switch model + retry
```

See [`docs/how-it-works.md`](docs/how-it-works.md) for the full mechanism, including the root
cause analysis and a reproducible controlled experiment.

---

## Verify

```sh
ocf-doctor                                     # or ./doctor.sh
# / or:
opencode plugin list                           # "nul-sanitizer" must be listed
python3 ~/.config/opencode/scripts/fix-nul-bytes.py --dry-run
tail ~/.config/opencode/nul-sanitizer.log      # what the plugin actually did
```

Expected: the plugin is listed and no NUL bytes are reported.

### Proof it actually works

Controlled experiment on a real install — one session, one injected NUL, the plugin as the only
variable, against a provider that rejects NUL bytes:

```
plugin OFF + NUL in history ->  finish=error  provider.invalid-request   (the bug)
plugin ON  + same NUL       ->  finish=stop   + log: "scrubbed NUL bytes from 1 string(s)"
```

For the removed-model path: a session pinned to a delisted model
(`opencode/exo-free`) is switched to the configured fallback and completes normally.

---

## Uninstall

```sh
./uninstall.sh
# or, from anywhere:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CanArslanDev/opencode-invalid-request-fix/main/uninstall.sh | bash
```

Removes the plugin, the script and the managed `AGENTS.md` block. Your own `AGENTS.md` content and
all session data are left untouched.

---

## Requirements

- macOS or Linux, `bash`, `curl`, `python3`
- OpenCode **v2** (plugin API `@opencode/plugin`)
- No network at run time; everything is local

## Limitations / notes

- The plugin only fixes the **outgoing** request. Your database may still contain NULs — harmless,
  and `/fix-nuls` cleans them if you care.
- If OpenCode ships a breaking plugin-API change, re-check with `opencode plugin list` after
  upgrading. See [`docs/troubleshooting.md`](docs/troubleshooting.md).
- The deprecated-model recovery needs a usable default model. Keep `model` in `opencode.json`
  pointing at something that exists, or set `OPENCODE_NUL_FALLBACK_MODEL=provider/model`.
- It does not help with unrelated 400s (oversized payloads, provider outages).

## Credits

Root cause found while debugging a real Ableton Live cracking session that kept dying on
`grep -a` over binary files. Reverse-engineered from that incident.

# The NUL byte problem (managed block)

`grep -a`, `cat`, `head` and `tail` over **binary** files (binaries, `.pyc`, `.db`,
log files, app bundles ...) leak `\x00` (NUL) bytes into tool results. Some
providers (e.g. Venice) then reject every later request in that session with:

```
400 Invalid request parameters — String must not contain null bytes
```

Once the NUL is in the stored history, "continue" does not help.

**Rule — filter binary output at the source:**

```sh
grep -a "pattern" file | tr -d '\000'
strings -a file | grep "pattern"
tail -5 file | tr -d '\000'
```

A global `nul-sanitizer` plugin already scrubs NUL bytes right before every model
call, so forgetting the filter is not fatal — it just keeps payloads smaller.

If NULs are already in the history, clean them permanently with `/fix-nuls`
(add `dry` to only report).

# Changelog

## 1.0.0 — 2026-10-31

Initial release.

- `nul-sanitizer` plugin:
  - scrubs `U+0000` from `messages`/`system` before every model call
    (`context`, `compaction`, `generate`, `title`),
  - `prompt` hook: admission-time guard that repairs a session pinned to a
    delisted model (`ModelUnavailableError` / `provider.no-route`),
  - `retry` hook: retries `provider.invalid-request` up to 3 attempts and recovers
    from `410 ModelDeprecated` by switching to the fallback model,
  - appends diagnostics to `<config>/nul-sanitizer.log`
    (silence with `OPENCODE_NUL_QUIET=1`).
- `/fix-nuls` TUI command plus `scripts/fix-nul-bytes.py` for permanent database
  cleanup with backup and `integrity_check`.
- `install.sh` (works via `curl | bash` or from a clone, idempotent, backs up
  existing files), `uninstall.sh`, `doctor.sh`.
- Managed `AGENTS.md` block so the agent filters binary output at the source.
- Verified with a controlled experiment: plugin off reproduces the exact
  `provider.invalid-request` failure; plugin on passes with the same history.

# How it works

## The failure

An OpenCode session can become permanently unusable: every new message (even
"continue") fails immediately with

```
Error: Invalid request parameters
400  {"issues":[{"message":"String must not contain null bytes","path":["messages",183,"content"]}]}
```

The session is fine, the model is fine, the prompt is fine. The **stored history**
contains a character the provider's validator refuses: a NUL byte (`U+0000`).

## Where the NUL bytes come from

Any command that prints a *binary* file can emit NUL bytes into a tool result:

```sh
grep -a "pattern" Preferences.cfg        # `-a` = treat binary as text, but NULs pass through
grep -a -o -E ".{80}pattern.{120}" x.pyc
cat Library.cfg
tail -5 Log.txt
```

`strings` is safe; `grep -a`, `cat`, `head`, `tail` are not.

Once that tool result is persisted, the NUL lives in the conversation. Providers
differ:

| Provider behaviour | Result |
|---|---|
| tolerates NUL in message content | session keeps working (NUL stays behind silently) |
| rejects NUL (e.g. Venice) | `400`, and **every** later request fails |

Because the offending character is in the *history*, not in the new message,
retrying with the same history reproduces the same error forever. That is why
"devam et" / "continue" never rescued the session.

## Why hooking the request is the right place

Persisted history would have to be rewritten for every broken session, and any
new NUL would break the session again until someone noticed.

The plugin instead hooks the moment right before dispatch:

```ts
await ctx.session.hook("context", onRequest)      // agent loop + tool continuations
await ctx.session.hook("compaction", onRequest)   // checkpoint summaries
await ctx.session.hook("generate", onRequest)     // transient generations
await ctx.session.hook("title", onRequest)        // title generation
```

`onRequest` walks `event.messages` and `event.system` and replaces `"\u0000"` with
`" "`. The documented contract for these hooks is that changes affect only the
outgoing model call and never the stored history — which is exactly what we want:

- new sessions can never break from a NUL,
- **old broken sessions start working again immediately**,
- no database surgery is required.

The database cleanup script and the `/fix-nuls` command exist only as
housekeeping (smaller payloads, clean `doctor` output).

## The controlled experiment

Reproduced on a real install. One session, one injected NUL in the history, the
plugin as the only variable:

| Plugin | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ON | history contains a NUL | `finish=stop` |
| **OFF** | same history | `finish=error`, `provider.invalid-request` |
| ON | same history | `finish=stop` |

The middle row is the bug; the first and last rows are the fix.

Caveat worth knowing: this only shows the bug against a provider that rejects NUL
bytes. On the same machine a *local* OpenAI-compatible proxy tolerated them and all
three rows passed — the fix is provider-independent, but a reproduction needs a
strict provider (Venice's hosted API, for example).

## Second cause: a removed model (`410` / `provider.no-route`)

A session stores the model it was created with. If that model disappears from the
catalogue, the session fails — and again it is sticky, because the model is pinned
in the session row. Two shapes exist:

- `410` + `Model <id> has been deprecated.` (the provider answers)
- `ModelUnavailableError` / `provider.no-route` + `Model unavailable: provider/model`
  (the request is never even built)

The second shape happens *before* the request exists, so a `retry` hook never sees
it. That is why there are two layers:

1. **`prompt` hook (admission-time guard).** On every incoming prompt the session's
   model is compared against the live model list. If it is gone, the session is
   switched to the fallback before the request is assembled.
2. **`retry` hook.** Catches `provider.no-route` and `410` that slip through, switches
   the session and retries (max 3 attempts).

The fallback is resolved from:

1. `OPENCODE_NUL_FALLBACK_MODEL=provider/model`, else
2. `model` in `opencode.json` / `opencode.jsonc`.

`ctx.session.switchModel` persists, so the session is repaired, not just retried.

## Diagnostics

`console.log` from a server plugin is not written to `opencode.log`, so the plugin
appends to `<config>/nul-sanitizer.log` instead — every scrub and every model repair
is recorded there. Set `OPENCODE_NUL_QUIET=1` to silence it.

## Scope and honesty

- Only `U+0000` is rewritten. Other control characters a provider might dislike
  are left alone.
- The NUL scrubbing is unconditional and cheap: with no NULs in the payload
  nothing is written back.
- The `retry` hook is capped at 3 attempts to avoid loops.
- If the fallback model equals the removed model, no switch happens and the
  request is not retried pointlessly.
- Nothing leaves the machine; there is no runtime network dependency.

# Troubleshooting

Run `./doctor.sh` first — it reports NUL bytes, failed sessions and sessions
pinned to a removed model.

## The plugin is installed but not active

Check what the server actually loaded:

```sh
opencode plugin list
```

If `nul-sanitizer` is missing:

```sh
opencode service restart
opencode plugin list
```

A plugin whose file is newer than the running server still gets picked up by the
config watcher, but a restart is the reliable way after a fresh install.

## Sessions still fail after installing

1. Confirm the plugin is loaded (above).
2. Look at what the plugin actually did:

   ```sh
   tail -20 ~/.config/opencode/nul-sanitizer.log
   ```

3. Confirm the failure is really the NUL one:

   ```sh
   ./doctor.sh
   ```

4. If new failures mention something other than `null bytes`, `deprecated` or
   `unavailable`, they are outside this repo's scope — check `opencode.log` for the
   provider response body.

## The `/fix-nuls` command does nothing

- Commands come from plugins, so the plugin must be loaded.
- `/fix-nuls dry` only reports; plain `/fix-nuls` writes (after taking a backup).
- The command needs `python3` on `PATH`.

## Disk usage from backups

Every cleanup writes `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db.bak-nul-<stamp>`
(~30 MB each). Keep the last few:

```sh
ls -1t ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db.bak-nul-* | tail -n +4 | xargs rm -f
```

## `opencode.json` lost its comments

`install.sh --model` rewrites `opencode.json` as plain JSON. If you had JSONC
comments in that file, they are dropped. Pass `--no-agents` and edit `model`
manually if you need to keep them.

## Manual repair without the plugin

```sh
sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
  "UPDATE session_message SET data = replace(data, '\u0000', ' ');"
```

SQLite does not interpret backslash escapes, so `'\u0000'` here is the literal
six-character escape that is stored in the JSON text. Prefer the bundled script,
which also takes a backup and re-validates the JSON.

## After an OpenCode upgrade

A breaking plugin-API change shows up as a load error in
`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` and `opencode plugin list` no longer
listing the plugin. Check the [plugin docs](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/server)
and update, or open an issue.

## Uninstall

```sh
./uninstall.sh
```

Removes the plugin, the script and the managed `AGENTS.md` block only. Session
data and backups are kept.

## The removed-model recovery did not trigger

It needs a fallback that exists:

```sh
export OPENCODE_NUL_FALLBACK_MODEL=provider/model
```

or keep `model` in `opencode.json` set to something currently listed by
`opencode models`.
